requirement: Empty successful process cannot satisfy requested test execution

files.note: Deliberately does not match GUT's test_*.gd naming convention, so -gdir=res://tests selects a real, populated, existing directory with zero matching tests -- not an ambiguous empty directory.

inputs.name: default
inputs.prerequisite: godot --headless --path . --import (once, to build the project's global class cache; GUT uses class_name declarations that gut_cmdln.gd checks for on startup)

measured_with_gut_9_7_1.console_output:
[GUT ERROR]:  Nothing was run.
On the one hand nothing failed, on the other hand nothing did anything.
measured_with_gut_9_7_1.finding: GUT itself correctly classifies this as an ERROR-level condition in its console log, and a JUnit XML artifact (when requested via -gjunit_xml_file) correctly records tests="0" -- both are honest. But the raw process exit code is 0 (success) regardless, traced to addons/gut/gui/GutRunner.gd's _handle_quit(): exit_code only becomes non-zero when gut.get_fail_count() > 0, and a run with zero tests has zero failures by construction. A harness or CI pipeline that gates on exit code alone -- the most common integration pattern -- will treat a zero-test run as a passing build.
measured_with_gut_9_7_1.requirement_met: partially -- the tool's own reporting is honest, but its process-level success signal (exit code) is not, which is the signal most external automation actually checks.

notes: This is a real, verified finding against the actual pinned GUT v9.7.1, not gd-tools -- GUT is the test-runner layer gd-tools' coverage workflow sits on top of, so this gap is inherited by any coverage adapter built on GUT's exit-code contract. The harness requirement this establishes: never gate a 'did tests run' check on process exit code alone; parse either the console for the 'Nothing was run' error or the JUnit/other structured artifact's test count.

reviewer: independent review agent (fable), 2026-09-19: re-ran both the default and JUnit-artifact inputs after --import: console output, exit code 0, and JUnit tests="0" all reproduce exactly; GutRunner.gd's _handle_quit confirmed to only set a non-zero exit code when get_fail_count() > 0.
ambiguities: Not tested: whether GUT's -gexit_on_success option or a nonstandard -gselect pattern (matching zero tests within an otherwise-populated, correctly-named set) produces different exit-code behavior than an empty -gdir selection. This fixture covers the directory-selection case only.

gd-tools' own pre_run_hook.gd/post_run_hook.gd wrap GUT's execution for coverage purposes; whether gd-tools' own wrapper adds an independent zero-test check on top of GUT's exit code is untested and belongs in BP04's real adapter run.
